newsitem.title: USA: NFL-PARCELLS, KRAFT TRY TO END DISTRACTION.
newsitem.headline: NFL-PARCELLS, KRAFT TRY TO END DISTRACTION.

text.p: New England head coach Bill Parcells and owner Robert Kraft made a joint appearance Wednesday to try and dissipate the black cloud that has hung over the Patriots this Super Bowl week.

Both have been annoyed by repeated questions about published reports saying Sunday's Super Bowl would be Parcells's last game with the Patriots due to a supposed rift between the owner and his head coach.

One report had Parcells paying more than a million dollars to get out of his contract, while another said Kraft would demand high draft picks as compensation for losing his coach, which could be the number one overall selection if Parcells jumps to the New York Jets as widely rumoured.
"There's been a little bit kind of swirling around," Parcells said, insisting this would be his final statement on the matter this week.
"Bob and I agreed a long time ago that we would go through this year and we would discuss the situation about the future when the season is over.
"And we're going to do that as expeditiously as possible, and I also can assure you that it's going to be done in a very civil and very friendly manner," Parcells said.
"That was our agreement and we're going to do that as soon as our season is over."

Kraft has been upset that rumours of Parcells's imminent departure has taken away from the momentous accomplishment of New England reaching the Super Bowl for the first time in 11 years and the first time under Kraft's watch.
"The fans in New England deserve for all of the focus to be on this game," Kraft has said.
On Wednesday, apparently pleased by Parcells's statement, Kraft was in a joking mood.

"We negotiated all night and I'm happy to announce that Bill Parcells has signed a 10-year contract to be the new manager of our paper and packaging group, Rand Whitney and International Forest Products," joked the paper magnate, who has said he wants Parcells back, but has refused to hand over total control of the team to his coach.
Getting a bit more serious, Kraft thanked Parcells despite "everything that's been stirred up over the last week."
"We bought the team three years ago yesterday," said Kraft, a longtime Patriots season ticket holder, "and here we are in the Super Bowl.
"There's a pretty special karma going on and we're excited about it and I thank you for this opportunity," Kraft said to Parcells.
